items.heading: If You Are Mapping Out
items.text: If you are mapping out a UX design career path for India, stop treating it as a list of screens to design and start treating it as a repeatable process: understand a real user problem through research, structure a solution through wireframes, test that structure in a rough prototype, only then apply visual design, and document the whole thing as a case study a stranger can follow. Tools, certificates, and job titles come after that process is real, not instead of it.

items.heading: Tools Change Faster Than Skills
items.text: Tools change faster than skills do, so the goal is fluency in one solid tool per category, not a checklist of every brand name on a job description.

rows: Builds three end-to-end portfolio projects as part of the course, which is the real value, not the certificate line on a resume. An Indian graduate survey reported strong positive career outcomes within six months of completion, but outcomes still depend on the quality of the projects you finish, not just enrollment.
Strong for building real UX theory and research method knowledge at a relatively low cost, useful alongside hands-on project work rather than as a replacement for it.
Short paid "become a UX designer in weeks" ad-funnel courses
Many of these are marketing-led rather than curriculum-led. Check for a real syllabus, real mentor access, and real project outcomes before paying, not just testimonials in the ad itself.
A four-year design degree (NID, IDC-IIT Bombay, and similar)
Worth it for the right stage and budget
Strong for depth, studio culture, and placement access if you are choosing this at the right life stage and can afford the time and cost. It is not a requirement to enter UX design professionally.

items.heading: Show Two to Three Case
items.text: Show two to three case studies as a junior candidate, and three to five once you have real work experience, not more.

items.heading: Structure Every Case Study Around
items.text: Structure every case study around the problem, your research, the options you considered, the decision you made, and the measured or observed outcome, not just the final screens.

items.heading: Include At Least One Project
items.text: Include at least one project with real usability testing evidence, even informal testing on five people, since this is what separates a UX portfolio from a UI-only one.

items.heading: Get Outside Feedback From
items.text: Get outside feedback from a working designer before you finish a project, not after you have already built the same mistake into three projects.
